messages:
Marco: Heads-up — running into a problem using the JS SDK inside a Next.js middleware (Edge runtime). Getting `ReferenceError: process is not defined` and `TypeError: require is not a function` when the middleware imports the SDK. Anyone seen this pattern?
Ivy: Yup, Edge runtime strips Node globals. Did you bundle an ESM-only build or are you importing the SDK's CJS entry?
Marco: We're pulling `@redwood/inference` (dev package name) via `import inference from '@redwood/inference'` in middleware.ts. The package currently has both cjs/esm exports but Next seems to pick the CJS one at build time and it tries to use `process.env` and `Buffer`.
Sam: In Next middleware you need the runtime: 'edge' and no Node builtins. Two quick checks: 1) does the SDK export a pure ESM/browser build that uses globalThis.fetch, crypto, etc? 2) Any use of fs/crypto/node:crypto?
Marco: It's using WebCrypto when available but falls back to node:crypto for HMAC in some code paths. That fallback is the culprit.
Becca: Workarounds we've used: a) force ESM-only import path (e.g. `import inference from '@redwood/inference/esm'`) if package ships that, b) use a tiny shim that replaces `node:crypto` usages with Web Crypto calls at build time, c) run SDK calls from an API route (server runtime) instead of middleware if feasible.
Ivy: Also check package.json "exports" field. If the package's conditional exports prefer cjs for Node, Next can still resolve the CJS entry even in edge builds. We had to publish a separate "edge" entry (`exports['./edge']`) that points to a minimal ESM file.
Marco: Is there a good way to detect the Edge runtime at build so we can switch imports? I thought dynamic import would help but Next complains about top-level dynamic import in middleware sometimes.
Sam: One pattern: create a tiny adapter file that only uses features allowed in the edge runtime — e.g. /lib/edge-inference.ts which re-exports from the ESM edge build. Then import that adapter from middleware. That keeps your app code explicit about edge compatibility.
Marco: Example adapter that worked for me:
```ts
// lib/edge-inference.ts
export { default } from '@redwood/inference/esm-edge';
```
Then in middleware: `import inference from '../lib/edge-inference';`
Becca: Another gotcha: Next's SWC bundler will inline `process.env` replacements at build time, but `process` itself is undefined at runtime. Avoid touching `process` at runtime in any code path imported by middleware. Use `process.env` only in files that run at build-time or in server routes.
Ivy: For auth tokens, prefer passing them via headers at middleware invocation time rather than reading env vars inside the imported module. Eg. `middleware(req) { const token = req.headers.get('x-rd-token'); }` keeps the module edge-safe.
Marco: Ok — switched to explicit edge export + adapter and removed node:crypto fallback. Now I'm seeing a `TypeError: fetch is not a function` coming from the SDK's internal fetch wrapper. Any tips?
Sam: Edge runtime exposes a global fetch but sometimes packages wrap it with undici/node-fetch detection. Ensure the SDK uses `globalThis.fetch` and doesn't import `node-fetch`. If it imports `node-fetch` conditionally, the bundler might include the wrong branch.
Becca: We added a very small patch in the SDK: prefer `const _fetch = typeof globalThis.fetch === 'function' ? globalThis.fetch : fetchPolyfill;` and exported an `edge` build that inlines `globalThis.fetch`. Published as `@redwood/inference/esm-edge` so apps can import explicitly.
Marco: That fixed it — middleware now runs and calls the inference API. :tada: A few follow-ups I noted: 1) types in TS sometimes break because project tsconfig uses `module: commonjs`. Recommend examples in the SDK repo showing `module: esnext` and `target: es2022` for edge projects.
Ivy: Agreed. Also include a tiny Next.js middleware example in the DX docs that shows the adapter, runtime: 'edge' in middleware config, and notes about env vs headers.
devex-bot: Reminder: file a tiny docs PR with the adapter snippet and the "exports.edge" recommendation so we can link from the README.
Marco: Will open a PR after lunch with the adapter example + note about WebCrypto fallback removal. Thanks everyone.
Becca: If you want, drop the failing stack trace here and I can sketch the minimal patch that toggles crypto implementation based on `typeof globalThis.crypto` so it doesn't import `node:crypto` at module eval time.
Marco: I'll paste it in the PR. Appreciate the help!
